currentFormal.channelAssignment: B if B.pass; else A if A.pass

A.structuralMeaning: A channel has a second hidden effective gate from signal-grade rejection beyond A.pass.

B.gradeACondition: formula >=80; many valid combinations satisfy this
B.structuralMeaning: B.pass itself already guarantees setupQuality above the B-grade threshold.

structuralFindings: Channel A/B and signal grade A/B are separate concepts with overlapping labels, creating semantic ambiguity.
Signal grade ignores five of the six base PriorityScore component families plus market-consensus bonus; it is a setup-quality grade, not an overall candidate-quality grade.
The >=65 grade gate is redundant for B but materially restrictive for A.

A-grade status is structurally much harder for A channel because A maximum is only 82; A-grade requires volumeTodayVsPrev5<=0.9 and combined pullback deviation plus support distance <=0.667 percentage points.
A candidate can have high PriorityScore because of fundamentals/institutions/sector/RS/RR but remain B-grade or be rejected if setupQuality<65.
A candidate can be A-grade on setup alone even if its other quality components are only minimally passing, because grade does not inspect them.
prospectiveTests: Grade distribution by channel and scanDate.
Fraction of A.pass rows rejected solely because setupQuality<65.
Fraction of B.pass rows ever below 65; expected structural zero unless formula/input semantics differ.
Outcome calibration of grade A vs B within each channel separately.
PriorityScore distribution conditional on signal grade; test discordant cells such as high PriorityScore/B-grade and low PriorityScore/A-grade.
Capital allocation by grade to determine whether user-visible grade aligns with actual risk/capital exposure.
Do not pool channel A-grade and channel B-grade until within-channel calibration is established.
falsification: If signal grade predicts path quality within both channels after controls, retain it as a setup-grade label even if not overall-quality grade.
If grade adds no value beyond raw setupQuality, treat letter grade as presentation only.
If cross-channel A/B grade comparisons are not calibrated, do not use the same letter as a cross-channel quality claim.
No threshold or label change before prospective evidence.
